issues.description: Condition reads awkwardly; a named helper would be clearer than inline negation.
issues.detail: `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` works but reads like a puzzle inside an already-dense boolean. A one-liner helper `isLayerStatement(node)` or `hasLayerBlock(node)` makes the intent obvious at the call site. Not a blocker — the patch is small, scoped, and tested — but the next maintainer will appreciate the rename.

issues.description: Use `node.nodes === undefined` or check `node.nodes == null` for consistency with PostCSS idioms.
issues.detail: `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` is defensive against the global `undefined` being shadowed, which isn't a real concern in this codebase. The rest of the file (and PostCSS in general) checks container-ness more directly. Match the existing style of the surrounding code rather than introducing a new idiom for one line.

issues.description: Test coverage misses `@layer foo;` (statement form) staying valid before `@import`.
issues.detail: The new test covers the bug (layer-with-block before import is rejected), but there should be a paired accept case proving the statement form `@layer foo;` before `@import` still passes. Without it, a future refactor could regress the original allowed behavior and no test would catch it. One extra fixture, three lines.

review.summary: Small, scoped, correct patch. It does exactly one thing: distinguishes `@layer foo;` (statement, allowed before `@import` per the CSS spec) from `@layer foo {}` (block, not allowed). Diff is readable, changeset is present, a regression test is included. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK only because the boolean would land cleaner as a named predicate and the accept-case for the statement form should be pinned down by a test. ACCEPT-after-trivial-fixup territory.
